Q0140

“If one hears the Way in the morning…” — Confucius (Analects 4.8)

Verified English quotation. Primary source: Analects 4.8. Theme: way.

Quotes / Confucius / Q0140

English

The Master said: If one hears the Way in the morning, one may die content that evening.
Thinker Confucius
School Confucianism
Source Analects 4.8
Theme Way

Context and commentary are editorial aids for reading. They do not replace the primary text or scholarly commentary.

Source and attribution

The archive attributes this English wording to Analects 4.8 and files it under Confucianism. That locator distinguishes the passage from loose internet attributions: readers can return to the named work or section to check translation, surrounding argument, and edition-specific wording.

About Confucius

Confucius (Kong Qiu, 551–479 BCE) taught in the late Spring and Autumn period amid the Zhou order’s political fragmentation. Born in the state of Lu, he briefly held local office and then spent years seeking rulers who would adopt ritual-based, virtue-centered government.

How to read this passage

Across 4 recurring voices here (notably Laozi and Confucius), way is framed through Confucianism and Daoism. Some passages define way; others warn how it fails; still others relocate it inside habit, community, or language. This passage enters that discussion through way, inquiry, life.

Concepts in this quote

Way
Way appears in this archive as a live philosophical concern—not a slogan. These verified English passages show how thinkers treat way as a problem of judgment, practice, or explanation.
Inquiry
Inquiry is the disciplined pursuit of better questions and answers—philosophy as method rather than dogma.
Life
Philosophy quotes about life ask what makes a life good, meaningful, or worth examining—questions that drive ethics, religion, and everyday decision.
